ruleset.name: nitpicker-main-rules
ruleset.description: Nitpicker's PMD rules for main sources.

rule.name: ClassLoadEffect
rule.message: Do this work in a method that main or the framework calls after startup (a @Bean method, an ApplicationRunner) and pass the result in, or create it on first use in a lazy holder class: this call runs while its class loads (in a static field or block, an enum constant, the constructor or initializer of an instance created at load, or a method one of them calls), so it connects, starts threads, sleeps or touches files in whatever order classes load, and in every test that touches the class. Constants, loggers, Pattern.compile and collections can stay static, and the class with main is not checked.

rule.name: DefaultTimeZone
rule.message: ZoneId.systemDefault() and TimeZone.getDefault() read the default time zone of the JVM, so the result changes with the TZ or -Duser.timezone of the server. Pass a zone: ZoneId.of("UTC"), a configured zone, or the zone of an injected Clock (clock.getZone()).

rule.name: LegacyCalendarApi
rule.message: Calendar.getInstance() and new GregorianCalendar() without a time zone, and new SimpleDateFormat(...) without setTimeZone, read the default time zone and are not thread-safe. Use java.time with an explicit zone: Instant, or ZonedDateTime.now(clock), and a DateTimeFormatter with withZone(zone). rule.name: UriCreateDynamic
rule.message: URI.create throws IllegalArgumentException on a space, a non-ASCII character or any other character that is not encoded, so one odd stored, user or header value turns this call into an error response. Build the URI with an encoding builder (UriComponentsBuilder.fromUriString(base).path(path).queryParam(name, value).encode().build().toUri(), or new URI(scheme, host, path, fragment)), or parse the text where the failure is handled: new URI(text) with URISyntaxException caught, or URI.create(text) in a try that catches IllegalArgumentException. A constant or a project helper that does one of these is fine. A value read from configuration at startup also matches, because a bad value fails only at runtime.
